original_entries.name: Lithoresonance
original_entries.description:
You touch a stone object, and depending on its size, it begins to emit a unique sound or vibration. The effect varies based on the size of the stone:

Grain’s Whisper: A grain of sand emits a faint vibration, detectable only by you. It can alert you to the presence of nearby creatures that you can’t see.

Pebble’s Pulse: A pebble emits a rhythmic pulse felt by creatures within 30 feet, providing them with a sense of direction or alerting them to danger.

Stone’s Hum: A stone emits a low hum that can be heard up to 60 feet away. This sound can distract enemies or communicate with allies.

Crystal’s Chorus: A crystal resonates, emitting a sound that can be heard up to 100 feet away. This sound can distract enemies or communicate with allies.

Boulder’s Ballad: A boulder emits a deep, resonating sound that can be heard up to 300 feet away. This sound can intimidate enemies or signal allies.

Erratic’s Echo: An erratic (a large rock or boulder) emits a powerful echo that can be heard up to 600 feet away. This echo can serve as a warning signal or a call to arms.

original_entries.name: Geochemical Golem
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a mixture of rare earth elements worth at least 1,000 gp, which the spell consumes)
original_entries.description:
You draw upon the surrounding earth and rare earth elements, shaping and infusing them with arcane energy to create a Geochemical Golem. This golem acts as an ally and follows your commands, fighting on your behalf.

The Geochemical Golem is designed for combat and possesses unique abilities derived from the rare earth elements used in its creation. It can attack, defend, and perform complex tasks as directed.

The Geochemical Golem remains in this form for the duration of the spell or until it drops to 0 hit points, at which point it crumbles back into the earth. If the golem is ever more than 100 feet away from you, it continues to follow the last command you gave it.

Elemental Infusion (page 62): You can customize the golem's abilities based on the situation and your preference. You need to have atleast full worth of one element, to gain the effect. You can combine and mix the elements, if you want to.

Basic combination: You can combine up to two different elements for the base casting cost of the spell. The total cost would be the sum of the individual elements chosen.

Advanced combination: For additional element beyond two, you can add a third element for an additional 400 gp, the forth element for an additional 2000 gp.

When you cast this spell using an 8th-level spell slot, the duration is 15 days.

When you cast this spell using a 9th-level spell slot, the duration is a month and a day.

You don't need to concentrate on this spell after 1 hour, when you cast it at higher levels.

original_entries.description: You channel the strength of the mountains, your size doubles in all dimensions, your current health is multiplied by four and your weight is multiplied by eight. This growth increases your size by one category. If there isn't enough room for you to double your size, you attain the maximum possible size in the space available. Your weapons also grow to match your new size. While these weapons are enlarged, your attacks with them deal 1d4 extra damage.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the extra damage increases by 1d4 for each slot level above 6th.
original_entries.source_notes: The original multiplies current health but does not specify how to restore current or maximum HP when the spell ends.

original_entries.name: Petalguard
original_entries.casting: 1 reaction, which you take when you or a creature within 60 feet of you takes damage
original_entries.description: You create a barrier of blossoming flowers around a creature. The creature gains resistance to all damage until the start of your next turn.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the duration increases by 1 round for each slot level above 6th.

original_entries.name: Stone Sentinel
original_entries.description: You cause a stone statue to rise from the ground in an unoccupied space you can see within range. The statue provides half cover to anyone behind it and can be commanded to move up to 30 feet as a bonus action on your turn.
original_entries.higher_levels:
When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level, the duration is 1 day.

When you use an 8th-level spell slot, the duration is 1 month.

When you use a 9th-level spell slot, the duration is 1 year and a day.

original_entries.name: Stone's Simphony
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a small stone instrument)
original_entries.description: Drawing from the harmonious sounds that stones can produce, you play a symphony that inspires your allies. Each ally within a 30-foot radius gains advantage on attack rolls, saving throws, and ability checks until the end of your next turn.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the range increases by 5 feet for each slot level above 6th.
original_entries.source_notes: The body heading reads Stone's Simphony; the page-40 spell index reads Stone's Simphony as well.

original_entries.name: Unstoppable Force
original_entries.description: You transform into a living mountain and charge at a creature you can see within range. The creature must make a Strength saving throw, taking 5d10 bludgeoning damage and being knocked prone on a failed save, or half as much damage and not being knocked prone on a successful one.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 6th.

original_entries.name: Wind's Gale
original_entries.description: A line of strong wind 60 feet long and 10 feet wide blasts from you in a direction you choose. Each creature that starts its turn in the line must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spellcasting DC or be pushed 15 feet away from you in a direction following the line. Any creature in the line must spend 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves when moving closer to you. The gust disperses gas or vapor, and it extinguishes candles, torches, and similar unprotected flames in the area. It causes protected flames, such as those of lanterns, to dance wildly and has a 50 percent chance to extinguish them.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the length of the line increases by 10 feet, and the width of the line increases by 5 feet for each slot level above 6th.
original_entries.source_notes: The printed duration is Instantaneous, although the rules also refer to creatures starting turns in the line. Preserved for review without choosing a duration.

original_entries.name: Crystal Mirror
original_entries.description: You create a large, flat crystal mirror that floats in the air in front of you. Any spell of 4th level or lower cast at you from the mirror's direction is reflected back at the caster. If the spell can't target the caster, it simply fails.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th level or higher, the spell level, which can be reflected, increases by 1 for each slot level above 7th.

original_entries.name: Dunesurge
original_entries.description: You create a swirling vortex of sand at a point you can see within range. Each creature in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Constitution saving throw. A creature takes 10d6 slashing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The vortex lasts for the duration, and any creature that ends its turn in the vortex takes 4d6 slashing damage.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th level or higher, the radius of the sphere increases by 5 feet, and the damage increases by 2d6 for each slot level above 7th.
original_entries.source_notes: The printed duration is Instantaneous, but the vortex also lasts for the duration and deals end-of-turn damage. The source conflict is not resolved here.

original_entries.name: Lithic Echoes
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a small stone flute)
original_entries.description: Inspired by the echoes that resonate within stone structures, you cause the ground and walls around you to echo with a haunting melody. Each creature within a 30-foot radius must make a Wisdom saving throw or be frightened until the end of its next turn.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th level or higher, the range increases by 5 feet for each slot level above 7th.

original_entries.name: Geosync
original_entries.description: You become one with the earth, gaining the ability to move through nonmagical, unworked earth and stone as if it was air. While moving in this way, you do not disturb the material you move through. You also gain tremorsense out to a range of 30 feet. The spell ends if you end your turn inside a stone object or surface.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th level or higher, the duration increases by 1 minute for each slot level above 7th.

original_entries.name: Geomantic Unity
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a handful of soil)
original_entries.description:
You form a deep connection with the land around you, merging your consciousness with the natural world. For the duration, you gain the ability to manipulate natural features within a 1-mile radius of your location. You can cause the following effects:

Alter Terrain. You can raise or lower the terrain, creating hills, ditches, or flat land. The maximum height or depth is 10 feet per minute. This does not affect buildings or other structures.

Divert Water. You can change the course of rivers or streams, or dry them up entirely. You can also create springs in places where water is close to the surface.

Grow Vegetation. You can cause plants to grow rapidly. This can create thickets or clearings in forests, or cause crops to grow in fields. The plants grow naturally and require suitable conditions to survive.

You have no control over animals, weather, or any unnatural constructs within the area. Any changes you make using this spell are permanent and occur naturally, though they may be startling or disruptive to those who witness them.
original_entries.higher_levels:
When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th level or higher, the radius of your control extends to 2 miles, and the speed at which you can alter terrain doubles.

When you cast this spell using a 9th level spell slot, the radius of your control extends to 3 miles, and the speed at which you can alter terrain triples. Additionally, you gain the ability to cause minor seismic activity, such as tremors, within the area of your control. These tremors aren't strong enough to cause damage but can be used to create distractions or unsettle creatures in the area.

original_entries.name: Neodrakite Net
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a net woven with threads infused with neodrakite worth at least 500 gp, which the spell consumes)
original_entries.description:
You create a shimmering net of rare earth elements and hurl it at a creature that you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be restrained for the duration. The net has no effect on creatures that are formless, or creatures that are Huge size or larger. The restrained creature can use its action to make a Strength check against your spell save DC.

Once ensnared, the neodrakite in the net begins to contract, exerting a crushing force on the restrained creature. At the start of each of its turns, the restrained creature takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage and the DC to escape the net increases by 1. The restrained creature can use its action to make a Strength check against the current DC. On a success, it frees itself.
original_entries.higher_levels:
When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th level or higher, the size of the creature that the net can restrain increases by one size category for each slot level above 7th. At 9th level, the net can restrain Gargantuan creatures.

Additionally, the damage dealt at the start of the restrained creature's turns increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 7th.
original_entries.source_notes: The spell-list index on PDF page 40 calls this Neodymium Net; the body heading and material text on page 70 say Neodrakite Net. The printed higher-level size wording is retained.

original_entries.name: Petalrage
original_entries.components: V, S, M (radiant flowers worth atleast 500 gp, which the spell consumes)
original_entries.description: You create a burst of blossoming energy that explodes at a point you can see within range. Each creature in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 12d6 radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The radiant energy is so potent that it continues to burn the target for 1d6 radiant damage at the start of each of its turns for the next minute.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th level or higher, the radius of the sphere increases by 5 feet, and the damage increases by 2d6 for each slot level above 7th.

original_entries.name: Stone's Aegis
original_entries.components: V, S, M (atleast 50 pounds of stone)
original_entries.description: You are surrounded by a protective barrier of swirling stones. The barrier provides you with a +5 bonus to AC and deals 2d6 bludgeoning damage to any creature that hits you with a melee attack. The barrier moves with you, remaining centered on you and hedging out creatures that end their turn within 5 feet of you. They must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 bludgeoning damage.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th level or higher, the bonus to AC increases by 1, and the damage dealt to creatures that hit you with a melee attack increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 7th.

original_entries.name: Thorn Spitter
original_entries.description: You summon a plant that spits thorns at a creature within 60 feet radius of the plant, dealing 4d10 piercing damage.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 7th.
original_entries.source_notes: The original spell does not provide a plant statblock, attack roll or save, attack cadence, or complete control rules. Those omissions are preserved here; the separately converted monster option is an adaptation.

original_entries.name: Elemental Surge
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a crystal worth at least 100 gp)
original_entries.description: You touch a crystal and cause it to radiate a brilliant light. Each creature of your choice that you can see within range regains hit points equal to 8d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier, and it is freed from any curse, disease, poison, blindness, or deafness.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 9th level, the healing increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 8th.

original_entries.name: Geomorph's Wisdom
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a diamond encrusted trowel worth at least 5,000 gp, which the spell consumes)
original_entries.description: You touch the ground and imbue it with the power to reshape itself according to your will. For the duration, you can use your action to cause the land within a 500-foot radius of you to alter its form, creating new geographical features such as hills, valleys, rivers, or even small mountains. The extent of the change is up to you, but the land must end up as a natural formation.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a 9th level spell slot, the duration is 8 hours, and the radius of land you can affect increases to 1,000 feet. Additionally, you can create more dramatic geographical features, such as a large mountain, a deep chasm, or a wide river.

original_entries.name: Geomorph's Stone Sentence
original_entries.description:
You point at a creature you can see within range and attempt to turn it into stone. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is instantly petrified, its form becoming a lifeless, solid statue. If the creature has 100 hit points or fewer, it is instantly killed as its entire form is converted into stone.

If the creature has more than 100 hit points, it takes 10d10 necrotic damage as parts of its body begin to turn to stone, and it is restrained. The creature must make another Constitution saving throw at the end of its next turn. If it fails, it is petrified. If it succeeds, the spell ends and the creature is no longer restrained.

A creature petrified by this spell remains in its stony state until freed by the greater restoration spell or other magic. Additionally, if the creature has 200 hit points or fewer, it is instantly killed and turned to stone. If the creature has more than 200 hit points, it is restrained and must make the additional Constitution saving throws as described above.
original_entries.source_notes: The source gives both immediate petrification and a delayed-save procedure, and both 100-HP and 200-HP instant-death thresholds. All conflicting text is retained for review; no threshold or procedure is selected.

original_entries.name: Petrified Resilience
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a staff made from petrified wood worth at least 500 gp)
original_entries.description:
You channel the ancient power of Geomorphy through your staff, causing it to resonate with a deep, earthy energy. Choose a target you can see within range. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target suffers the following effects for the duration:

The target takes 2d10 necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns as its body begins to harden and petrify.

The target has disadvantage on Strength-based weapon attack rolls due to the increasing weight and stiffness of its body.

Additionally, all allies within range receive a protective earth shield, reducing the damage they take by 15%. The deflected damage is dealt to the target.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a 9th level spell slot, the necrotic damage increases to 4d10, and the damage reduction increases to 20%.

original_entries.name: Prism Break's Gem Eruption
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a gemstone worth at least 500 gp)
original_entries.description:
You point at a location within range and cause a brilliant gem to erupt from the ground. All creatures within a 20-foot radius of the gem must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 8d10 radiant damage as they are bombarded with a dazzling array of refracted light, and they are blinded until the end of their next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't blinded.

The gem remains after the spell ends and can be used as a spellcasting focus. Additionally, the area within a 20-foot radius of the gem is brightly illuminated by refracted light for 1 minute, creating difficult visual conditions for creatures sensitive to light.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 9th level, the radius of the dazzling light and the area of effect increases to 30 feet, and the damage increases to 10d10 radiant damage. Furthermore, creatures that fail their saving throw are blinded until the end of their next two turns.

original_entries.name: Rock Tomb
original_entries.casting: 1 reaction, which you take when you are hit by an attack
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a small piece of stone)
original_entries.duration: Until the end of the attacker's next turn
original_entries.description: When you are hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to encase the attacker in rock, restraining them until the end of their next turn. The attacker must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the attacker is restrained by the rock tomb. On a successful save, the attacker is not restrained.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 9th level, the duration increases. The rock tomb now lasts until the end of the attacker's second turn after being encased. Additionally, the attacker takes 4d8 bludgeoning damage upon being encased, regardless of the saving throw result.

original_entries.name: Rockpause
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a gemstone worth at least 500 gp)
original_entries.description: You touch a willing creature, and it enters a state of suspended animation. Time ceases to flow for it, and it doesn't age.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 9th level, the creature is also immune to all attacks.

original_entries.name: Sandgrip
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a handful of desert sand)
original_entries.description: You cause the ground in a 100-foot radius within range to become a swirling sandstorm. The area becomes difficult terrain and visibility is reduced to 10 feet for the duration. Each creature that starts its turn in the area must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 4d10 bludgeoning damage and is restrained for the duration. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't restrained. A creature restrained by the sandstorm can use its action to make a Strength check against your spell save DC. On a success, it frees itself.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a 9th level spell slot, the radius of the sandstorm increases to 200 feet, and the damage increases to 6d10.

original_entries.name: Seismic Echo
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a shard of obsidian worth at least 500 gp)
original_entries.description:
You create a seismic wave at a point within range. All creatures in a 20-foot radius must make a Dexterity save. On a fail, they take 8d8 bludgeoning damage and are knocked prone, or half damage on a successful save. The ground becomes difficult terrain.

The seismic wave emits a loud echo, audible up to 600 feet away. While concentrating, you can use a bonus action on your turn to cause a secondary tremor, forcing creatures in the area to make the saving throw again.
original_entries.higher_levels: When cast at 9th level, the radius, damage, and echo range increase by 50%.

original_entries.name: Stoneform Titan
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a shard of ancient stone or a relic from a titan's remains)
original_entries.description:
You call upon the ancient and primordial power of the Tartas Titans, transforming yourself into a massive stone titan. For the duration, you gain the following benefits:

Size and Strength. Your size triples, and your weight multiplies by twenty. Your Strength score increases by 6, and your Constitution increases by 4. Your attacks with melee weapons deal an additional 2d6 bludgeoning damage.

Titan's Resilience. You gain resistance to non-magical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, and immunity to poison and petrification.

Earth Mastery. You can move through earth and stone as if it were air. You can also cause the ground to shake within a 30-foot radius, forcing creatures to make a Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

Wind Control. As a bonus action, you can summon a gust of wind, pushing creatures within a 15-foot cone away from you. A successful Strength saving throw negates this effect.

Primordial Roar. As an action, you can unleash a mighty roar that terrifies enemies. Creatures within a 60-foot radius must make a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened for 1 minute.

Titan's Grasp. Your reach increases by 10 feet, and you gain advantage on grapple checks.

Legendary Presence. Your appearance becomes awe-inspiring. You have advantage on Charisma checks and saving throws.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 9th level, the duration increases to 10 minutes, and you gain temporary hit points equal to your spellcasting ability modifier times your level.

original_entries.name: Summitsmash
original_entries.description: You cause the ground in a 40-foot-radius, 20-foot-high cylinder centered on a point you can see within range to explode. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 12d6 bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. In addition, nonmagical structures in the area take the same damage and are destroyed.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 9th level, the radius of the cylinder increases by 10 feet, and the damage increases by 2d6.
original_entries.source_notes: The printed spell type is "geomophy" rather than "geomorphy".

original_entries.name: Treetimber
original_entries.description: You summon a massive tree that smashes down on a creature you can see within range, dealing 5d10 bludgeoning damage.
original_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 9th level, the damage increases by 1d10.

original_entries.name: Geomantic Ascendancy
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a diamond encrusted with earth and soil worth at least 5,000 gp, which the spell consumes)
original_entries.description: You become an embodiment of the earth. For the duration, you gain immunity to physical and elemental damage, can move through earth and stone, sense creatures in contact with the ground within 60 feet. You can also communicate with earth elementals and know Terran.

original_entries.name: Geoshape
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a diamond worth at least 5,000 gp, which the spell consumes)
original_entries.description:
You touch a piece of earth or stone and infuse it with a surge of geomantic energy. The targeted area, which can be no larger than a 100-foot cube, is permanently altered in one of the following ways at your discretion:

Diamond Hardness. The area becomes as hard as diamond, increasing its AC to 25.

Malleable Earth. The area becomes incredibly soft, almost like clay, and can be easily shaped or molded by hand.

Vibrating Resonance. The area vibrates with a constant, low-frequency hum that can be felt but not heard. Any creature in contact with the area can't be surprised and has advantage on initiative rolls.

Levitating Terrain. The area levitates 10 feet off the ground and can hold up to 10,000 pounds of weight. More weight causes the area to slowly descend to the ground until the excess weight is removed.

Radiant Light. The area emits a bright light in a 120-foot radius and dim light for an additional 120 feet. The light is sunlight.

Absorbing Darkness. The area absorbs all light, creating a 60-foot radius of magical darkness. Darkvision can't penetrate this darkness, and no natural light can illuminate it. Only the area within 5 feet of a creature with this spell's effect can be illuminated by magical light.

Magic Magnet. Any spell of 5th level or lower cast within 100 feet of the area is automatically absorbed by it, causing the spell to fail and have no effect. If a spell of 6th level or higher is cast within 100 feet of the area, the caster must make a spellcasting ability check against your spell save DC. On a failed check, the spell is absorbed. On a successful check, the spell is cast as normal. The area can absorb a number of spell levels equal to twice your spellcasting level before the spell ends. Absorbing a spell doesn't remove it from the caster's mind; it merely wastes the spell slot expended.

Source of Life. Nonmagical plants in a 100-foot radius of the area become enriched and grow at four times their normal rate. Any food crops in the area yield four times the normal amount of food when harvested.

Titan's Fortress. The area forms into a fortress of your design, complete with walls, towers, and rooms. The fortress is permanent and can't be dispelled, but it can be destroyed by normal means.

original_entries.name: Nature's Avatar
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a handful of soil and a diamond worth at least 5,000 gp, which the spell consumes)
original_entries.description:
You become an avatar of nature, embodying the raw power of the earth. Your size becomes Huge, your Strength and Constitution scores become 30, and you gain immunity to all non-magical damage. You also gain resistance to all magical damage except psychic. Your AC becomes 22 due to a thick layer of bark-like skin.

You can make two slam attacks as an action, each dealing 4d10 bludgeoning damage plus your Strength modifier. As a bonus action, you can cause thorny vines to erupt from the ground in a 20-foot radius centered on a point you can see within 120 feet. Each creature in that area must make a Strength saving throw or be restrained by the vines until the spell ends. A creature restrained by the vines, or one that can touch the creature, can use its action to make a Strength check against your spell save DC. On a success, the target is freed.

As a movement action, you can merge with the earth and move up to your speed to a location you can see, then emerge from the earth at that point.

While transformed, you have the ability to cast the following spells without expending spell slots: Entangle, Barkskin, Stoneskin, Wall of Thorns, and Earthquake. You can cast one of these spells as a bonus action on each of your turns.

original_entries.name: Nature's Blessing
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a diamond worth at least 5,000 gp, which the spell consumes)
original_entries.description: You channel nature's ultimate power to heal and invigorate up to twelve creatures you can see within range. Each target is fully healed, cured of all diseases and conditions, and gains benefits of Greater Restoration and Heroes' Feast. They also gain resistance to all damage, +10 feet speed, and +2 to AC for one hour.

original_entries.name: Petroforce Ascendancy
original_entries.description: You gain a bonus to your Strength score equal to twice your spellcasting ability modifier for the duration.

original_entries.name: Promethium Portal
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a promethium-infused lodestone worth at least 5,000 gp, which the spell consumes)
original_entries.description:
You touch a large piece of stone within range and create a magical portal within it. Stepping through the portal transports you to another large piece of stone that you are familiar with, regardless of the distance separating the two. The destination stone must be on the same plane of existence as you, and it must be large enough to contain the portal (at least 5 feet in diameter).

The portal is two-dimensional and circular, with a diameter of up to 20 feet. You can orient the portal in any direction you choose. The portal remains open for the duration, and you can pass through it freely. Other creatures can also pass through the portal, but only if you give them permission.

original_entries.name: Sandsoverign
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a vial of sand from a desert, worth at least 1,000 gp)
original_entries.description:
You gain control over all sand within a 1-mile radius, allowing you to shape it as you wish. You can create structures, weapons, or other objects from the sand, but they cannot have any moving parts. The objects created by this spell are permanent and cannot be dispelled, but they can be destroyed by normal means.

In addition, you can command the sand to move and attack. As an action, you can cause a sandstorm within the area, dealing 4d10 bludgeoning damage to creatures of your choice that you can see within the area. Each creature must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking full damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Furthermore, you can use your action to cause the sand to form into a colossal sand golem under your command.
original_entries.source_notes: The source prints a Colossal Sand Golem statblock alongside this spell. The separately converted monster is available in the Monster manual. The spell does not specify a golem duration or active-count limit.

original_entries.name: Worldshaper's Command
original_entries.description: You gain the ability to reshape the landscape within a 1-mile radius centered on a point you can see within range. You can raise or lower the terrain, create or fill in bodies of water, and cause vegetation to grow or wither. Structures are not affected.

original_entries.name: Genesis
original_entries.components: V, S, M (a miniature model of the desired landscape, which the spell consumes)
original_entries.description: You create a new demiplane with a radius of up to 1 mile. The demiplane resembles any landform you choose; a desert, a forest, a mountain, a swamp, a tundra, etc. You determine the weather patterns, the presence of bodies of water, and the types of vegetation. The demiplane remains until you use this spell to banish it.

original_entries.name: Earth's Guidance
original_entries.draft_note: Listed in the source index; spell description missing from the supplied PDF.
original_entries.description: The page-40 Geomorphy spell list includes Earth's Guidance, but the spell-body pages do not provide a description under this name. Casting time, range, components, duration and effects need author text before this entry can be evaluated or adapted.
original_entries.source_notes: The separate Geomorpher's Compass body on page 41 is retained under its own title; no equivalence with Earth's Guidance is assumed.

original_entries.name: Stone's Embrace
original_entries.draft_note: Listed in the source index; spell description missing from the supplied PDF.
original_entries.description: The page-40 Geomorphy spell list includes Stone's Embrace, but the spell-body pages do not provide a description under this name. Casting time, range, components, duration and effects need author text before this entry can be evaluated or adapted.
original_entries.source_notes: Earth's Embrace and Stone's Resilience are separate printed spells; neither is silently substituted for this title.

annotated_entries.name: Breeze Whisper
annotated_entries.description: You whisper a message of twenty-five words or less to the wind, which carries it to a creature with which you are familiar. The creature hears the message in its mind and can reply in a like manner immediately. The spell doesn’t have to follow a straight line and can travel freely around corners or through openings.
annotated_entries.review: This is actually pretty great. I feel like there was a spell that was like this, but I couldnt find one so yeah. Should be a mystic cantrip.

annotated_entries.name: Gemstone's Glee
annotated_entries.description: You touch a gemstone and it begins to glow brightly, shedding bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be any color you choose.
annotated_entries.review: so, mystics or someone(I forgot) gets ennervate(or ennirvate?) which is similar, but this as a "light" cantrip would work great as an oath cantrip, but it might require a secondary effect, when compared to other cantrips. Given that oath cantrips are narrow, this having an extra option would be good.

annotated_entries.name: Geomorpher's Compass
annotated_entries.description: You touch the ground and commune with the earth, seeking guidance towards a known or clearly visualized destination. The earth subtly shifts beneath your feet, providing you with an intuitive sense of the direction you need to travel. This spell does not account for obstacles or dangers along the path, it merely provides the most direct route towards your destination.
annotated_entries.review: It should be a level 1 mystic spell. It might also need a range, and the name shouldnt include geomorpher, could just be compass. It cant be a cantrip really, as then it would get spammed and take up a lot of time where the player goes like "oh but what about this place? What direction is it if im standing here? What about here?" I dont know how you would fix that, but otherwise its not bad. It needds a good range if its going to be level one. Currently, this would be the earliest level "true info" spell, I believ, so dont assume that giving someone a skyrim marker makes it weak. But yeah, if you can fix that its legit good.

annotated_entries.name: Lithoresonance
annotated_entries.description:
You touch a stone object, and depending on its size, it begins to emit a unique sound or vibration. The effect varies based on the size of the stone:

Grain’s Whisper: A grain of sand emits a faint vibration, detectable only by you. It can alert you to the presence of nearby creatures that you can’t see.

Pebble’s Pulse: A pebble emits a rhythmic pulse felt by creatures within 30 feet, providing them with a sense of direction or alerting them to danger.

Stone’s Hum: A stone emits a low hum that can be heard up to 60 feet away. This sound can distract enemies or communicate with allies.

Crystal’s Chorus: A crystal resonates, emitting a sound that can be heard up to 100 feet away. This sound can distract enemies or communicate with allies.

Boulder’s Ballad: A boulder emits a deep, resonating sound that can be heard up to 300 feet away. This sound can intimidate enemies or signal allies.

Erratic’s Echo: An erratic (a large rock or boulder) emits a powerful echo that can be heard up to 600 feet away. This echo can serve as a warning signal or a call to arms.
annotated_entries.review:
once again, amazing mystic spell, but it cant be a cantrip. It could be a ritual spell though. the ranges need some work and im unsure if the "can intimidate" or  "can communicate" is well worded. im unsure also if it should have 6 options. Perhaps if it were limited to 3 options at lvl 1 as a ritual spell, and then at higher levels you might afford some other options. more like this:
you can do one of the following effects: whisper pebble: <some kind of new wording for an alarm-like effect. Obviously it cant be psychic the way classic alarm was.> noise stone: <some noise option> thunder rock: <maybe like throw it and it booms a little? and also noise. Maybe if you hit with it its noise, and it can be a sling/launcher projectile yknow.>
at higher levels:
  if cast with a 2nd lvl slot you can also do stone gong: <some kind of big signaling or alert thing. range should be decent. like idk mby a mile.>
  if cast with a 3rd lvl slot you can also do crystal resonance: <Only if its like a huge rock crystal or similar. Does some aura stuff idk.>
  If cast with a 4th lvl slot or higher, can also do mountain saga: <I honestly dont know, but it can include a scaling factor for even higher levels if necessary.>

annotated_entries.name: Magma's Ire
annotated_entries.description: You create a small shard of molten rock in your hand and hurl it at a creature you can see within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 fire damage and its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. This spell’s damage increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8), and 17th level (4d8).
annotated_entries.review: idk about this one. Im gonna vote no. its a different fire bolt. Also, throwing literal magma at someone is SO MUCH WORSE than 1d8 fire damage. The ability to summon magma at will at lvl 1 is also just... not ok at all. This is like the worst thing to do. 8D

annotated_entries.name: Mud Mire
annotated_entries.duration: Until the start of your next turn
annotated_entries.description: You choose a point within range and cause the ground in a 5-foot square centered on that point to become muddy and difficult to traverse. The area becomes difficult terrain until the start of your next turn.
annotated_entries.review: eeeeeh.... im gonna go with pass. Its a sub effect of mold earth which only lasts 1 round. If mystic spells should need a minor geomancy equivalent, it should have more than this.

annotated_entries.name: Pebble Pelt
annotated_entries.description: You summon and fling small rocks at a creature or object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage. The spell’s damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6), and 17th level (4d6).
annotated_entries.review: Also nah. I dont reall have a good reason why. Its just a rock throw thing. just throw a rock.

annotated_entries.name: Sand Veil
annotated_entries.description: You blend into the desert environment, gaining advantage on Stealth checks while you remain motionless.
annotated_entries.review: no. Too limited.

annotated_entries.name: Stone Whisper
annotated_entries.description: You touch a natural stone and receive a brief impression of a significant event that occurred around it within the past day.
annotated_entries.review: I like the idea of it. But it adds a ton of unnecessary game spam where the players just go around looking for stones and asking the GM to recreate the past day.  I dont know. It seems a bit wrong for a cantrip.

annotated_entries.name: Stone's Serenade
annotated_entries.description: You touch a stone and it begins to hum a soft, soothing melody. This melody can be heard up to 60 feet away and can calm beasts or provide comfort to allies.
annotated_entries.review: too similar to the other lithoresonance idea. Id say no to this one.

annotated_entries.name: Wind Slash
annotated_entries.description: You create a blade of wind and hurl it at a creature that you can see within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 slashing damage. This spell’s damage increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8), and 17th level (4d8).
annotated_entries.review: I... guess... im really not sure where this belongs. Its not bad. It might be a good mystic cantrip. I would say that it should then either require a focus or a slashin weapon.

annotated_entries.name: Blossom Burst
annotated_entries.components: V, S, M (petals and thorns worth 1 gp)
annotated_entries.classes: Bard, Cleric, Druid, Ranger, Sorcerer, Warlock
annotated_entries.description: You cause a small explosion of petals and thorns. Each creature in a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on a point you choose within range must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 2d8 piercing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 1st.
annotated_entries.review: I dont _really_ like it cus its sorta just a nature themed circle-blast spell. if there were a mystic or occult spell for exploding flowers, it should perhaps be more tied to having some nature-y focus or similar. And it might need more options due to the limitation then as a result. This should be reworked as a sub-ability of some higher level druid staff-like spell in the mystic spell class.
annotated_entries.source_notes: The source prints range Self while the description selects a point within range; this review entry preserves that wording.

annotated_entries.name: Boulder Pugilist
annotated_entries.description: Your fists become as hard as stone, making your unarmed strikes deal 1d6 bludgeoning damage on a hit.
annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 1st.
annotated_entries.review: The name is corny af and genuinely takes away from something that would otherwise be busted on monk. The thing is... its just busted on monk. I think if this were a part of the mystic spell list, it should be a sub-ability of smthn higher level. Like stone-skin.

annotated_entries.name: Crystal Cascade
annotated_entries.description: You conjure a cascade of sharp crystals that rain down on a location you specify. Each creature in a 10-foot-radius, 40-foot-high cylinder centered on a point within range must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 2d8 piercing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 1st.
annotated_entries.review: nah. Geometrically we should have a cylinder spell for sure, but this is too specific and too weird at an early level. I did notice the balancing trick, where you squeeze out more value by making it a large area but also a _weird_ area so its harder to use but technically balanced. But no I dont think this is gonna be it. Also, this is just summoning a bit of the blender universe in a location. that cant be a low level spell.

annotated_entries.name: Desert Mirage
annotated_entries.description: You create a 5-foot-radius sphere illusion of a desert oasis, potentially luring creatures towards it. Any creature that examines the illusion can determine that it is false with a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC.
annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the size of the illusion increases by 10 feet for each slot level above 1st.
annotated_entries.review: nah too specific, too limited, and in terms of magical ability, too powerful(weirdly) for such a low level. Should be achievable by a slightly higher or better illusion spell.

annotated_entries.name: Drumbeat of the Ancients
annotated_entries.components: V, S, M (a small drumstick made of bone)
annotated_entries.description: You beat a stone with a drumstick and cause it to resonate with a deep, sonorous tone. Each creature within a 15-foot radius must make a Wisdom saving throw or be stunned until the end of its next turn as the resonating sound overwhelms its senses.
annotated_entries.review: A stunbomb isnt a bad idea. But its too weirdly worded. I also think it shouldnt be stone themed. If it were differently themed or worded, it could be a lvl 1 oath spell.
annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot 2nd level or higher, the radius increases by 5ft for each slot level above 1st.

annotated_entries.name: Earth's Embrace
annotated_entries.description: You cause the ground in a 10-foot square within range to become difficult terrain.
annotated_entries.review: Not enough for what it is. Too narrow and specific. Its a spell slot for a multi-tile specific use of minor geomancy again. I just dont think its right/
annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the size of the square increases by 10 feet for each slot level above 1st.

annotated_entries.name: Flora's Blessing
annotated_entries.components: V, S, M (any plants worth 1 gp)
annotated_entries.description: You touch a willing creature and imbue them with the blessing of the flora, giving them advantage on Wisdom checks for the duration.
annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 1st.
annotated_entries.review: pretty sure advantage on specific saves is already a spell, but also an hour is a long time. I dont know, tbh. Like on paper a courage spell makes sense. It should be an oath spell, if one does not exist in that range. It should be renamed something else, though it shouldnt be named clarity or similar, as that is a condition. It doesnt have to be plant-themed, and idk if it should be _any_ plant worth 1gp, but it can be some kind of plant worth 1 gp to keep ir fresh.

annotated_entries.name: Gemstone Keenness
annotated_entries.components: V, S, M (a small piece of sharp gemstone)
annotated_entries.description: You touch a weapon and it becomes as sharp as a gemstone. For the duration, the weapon gets a bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls equal to your spellcasting ability modifier. The spell ends if you cast it again or if you let go of the weapon.
annotated_entries.review:
I like the idea of crushing gemstones for spells. It makes rewarding players with gems more useful. I think the higher level effect shouldnt exist, as then this lower level option starts stepping on the toes of other weapon enchantment spells. If it stays as just a special +1 to damage and attacks, it becomes compatible with +1 or similar bonuses to weapons.
so yeah, as an oath spell, crush a gemstone uppon your weapon(must be slashing or piercing I guess) to sharpen and enchant it for 1 minute. There should just be a lvl2 slot option that extends it to 10 minutes, and maybe a lvl 3 for 1 hour.
annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls increases by 1 for each two slot levels above the 1st.

annotated_entries.name: Geomantic Guidance
annotated_entries.components: V, S, M (a small piece of iron)
annotated_entries.description: This spell allows you to attune your senses to the geomantic forces of the earth. For the duration, you can accurately recall any path you have traveled.

annotated_entries.review: So this spell is basically a spell-known penalty for being able to say "nu uh" when the GM tells you that the BBEG blindfolded you. idk. I will lean towards no. I dont super see the utility in it, and most nature people are already great at tracking.

annotated_entries.name: Geomantic Pulse

The light illuminates a 30-foot radius with bright light and an additional 30 feet with dim light. You can choose the color of the light when you cast the spell. The light can be one color or can gradually shift through a spectrum of colors at your discretion.
annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot 2nd level or higher, the duration increases by 1 hour for each slot level above 1st.
annotated_entries.review: Naah, its too narrow. Its a torch as a spell slot.

annotated_entries.name: Leaf Armor
annotated_entries.description: You touch a willing creature and their skin toughens like bark, granting them a +1 bonus to AC for the duration.
annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 1st.
annotated_entries.review: Yeah this should probably be an oath spell. Its simplicity makes sense that it would be oath. idk about leag armor though. I would say, if it is "leaf armor" or "barkskin" or whatever then the target shouldnt be wearing heavy armor for it to work. Yknow? Otherwise id allow this one.

annotated_entries.name: Monolith's Mercy
annotated_entries.description: You call upon the strength of the earth, granting you and your allies within 10 feet temporary hit points equal to your spellcasting ability modifier. These temporary hit points last until the start of your next turn.

annotated_entries.review: Its literally a reskinned aoe temp HP effect. I think it should just exist as a normal aoe temp HP spell if one doesnt already exist. It makes sense to be oath, but im unsure if it should be level 1 as there might already be a basic single target temp HP spell at lvl 1. It depends. If this effect does not exist, then it should. But the earth theme just seems out of place.

annotated_entries.name: Petrified Pirrouette
annotated_entries.duration: Until the start of your next turn
annotated_entries.description: You perform a quick dance that causes the ground around you to ripple and shake, distracting your enemies within 10 feet and giving them disadvantage on their next attack roll against you.

annotated_entries.review: nah. since there is no bard list this just doesnt really have a place to be. Dance-casting should probably only stay in some archetype of bard, or bard-specific feat.

annotated_entries.name: Sandstorm Scourge
annotated_entries.description: You call forth a violent sandstorm in a 10-foot-radius, 20-foot-high cylinder centered on a point you can see within range. Each creature in the area must make a Constitution saving throw. A creature takes 2d8 slashing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 1st.
annotated_entries.review:
yeah but just cus you theme a mini-aoe effect with nature doesnt mean it mechanically belongs in the mystic spell list. It cant really be mystic(druid) The point isnt that they just tell nature what to do, its that they know or find or figure out the subtle or wild things that others dont. But as an arcane spell it seems too limited. If this were an effect, it should be some sub-effect of a higher level ethermancy(wind bending or smthn) effect Or, if it were to be made mystic, it would need to be higher level and would be something like "conjure whirlwind" and then depending on the terrain it has additional effects.
so final verdict is no for now.

annotated_entries.name: Sand's Shift
annotated_entries.casting: Reaction, which you take when you are hit by an attack
annotated_entries.description: You transform into sand to avoid an attack. The attack misses you, and you teleport up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the teleportation distance increases by 10 feet for each slot level above 1st.
annotated_entries.review: Reactions that let you use mobility are great. That said, this is misty step but sand themed. If theres gonna be a misty step, it should be misty step. Also misty step I think has more range, though im unsure if its lvl 1. As it stands, a sand option _could_be a higher level occult spell, but then it needs more. I will say, as it stands, this is a no, but we need a reaction -> move spell.

I cant explain why but it feels less bad if its wis than dex.  this is kind alike enhance ability and I just feel like we shouldnt print 6 versions of something if it can be a few. idk. worth discussing.

annotated_entries.name: Zephyr's Shield
annotated_entries.description: You summon a gust of wind that wraps around you or a creature you can see within range, giving a bonus to AC equal to your spellcasting ability modifier for the duration. The spell ends if you cast it again or if the creature is ever more than 60 feet away from you.

annotated_entries.revidew: eh idk. It steps on too many toes. Its different cus of the range limitation, but if you can pull someone out of a 60ft range, you can overcome a +1 bonus to AC. I think I will pass on this one.

Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 3d8 bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd.
annotated_entries.review: its another cylinder fireball. No. Also no cus if you can make force to make boulders explode, just do it inside the enemy. make his kidney stones explode.

annotated_entries.name: Crystalize
annotated_entries.description: You target a creature you can see within range, and its skin hardens to crystal. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 2d8 piercing damage and has its speed halved until the start of your next turn.
annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd.
annotated_entries.review: lol more like lesser petrify. Idk. Could be a lvl 2 occult spell. Or perhaps a lvl 2 mystic or oath spell but then it would need to have something else, cus they shouldnt be able to just make anyone crystalize willy nilly. Only occultists and arcane users should have that power. Also I think the name crystalize might be used, but im unsure. Otherwise it seems ok. I would suggest looking at some conditions to apply for fun. Such as maimed, hobbled, etc. perhaps make them last until the target somehow gains regeneration or is subject to lesser restoration. idk. If so, then it could be lvl 3 occult.

annotated_entries.name: Desert's Wrath

Each creature in the area must make a Constitution saving throw. A creature takes 3d8 slashing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd.

Each creature in the area must make a Strength saving throw or be restrained for the duration. A creature restrained by the hands can use its action to make a Strength check against your spell save DC. On a success, it frees itself.

annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd.
annotated_entries.review: duplicate of floral blessing or whatever, no? same answer.

annotated_entries.name: Frightful Monolith
annotated_entries.description: You quickly turn your face into frightful stone statue and instill a deep fear in a creature that attacks you, causing it to have disadvantage on attack rolls against you until the end of its next turn.
annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can increase the range by 10 feet for each slot level above 2nd.
annotated_entries.review: im unsure. needs work. There could be a spell in here but as it stands its a weird combo. Stone feels out of place, so it needs to have a different theme. Other than that, it also needs to be a bit more than, you attacked so now I fear you. I like the idea of reaction spells, and just for that I would be willing to allow it, but it needs some kind of adjusting first. I dont know what class it would belong to yet.

annotated_entries.name: Gemstone's Grace

annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the healing increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd.
annotated_entries.review: if were gonna add pay-to-win healing it should be more interesting. Steps on the toes of some healing spells and is overall just kinda whatevrer. as it stands, I say no.

The creature gains half cover, which provides a +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws. The barrier lasts for the duration or until it is destroyed. The barrier has AC 12 and 15 hit points.

annotated_entries.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the duration increase by 30 minutes for each slot level above 2nd.

annotated_entries.name: Geochemical Golem
annotated_entries.components: V, S, M (a mixture of rare earth elements worth at least 1,000 gp, which the spell consumes)

The Geochemical Golem is designed for combat and possesses unique abilities derived from the rare earth elements used in its creation. It can attack, defend, and perform complex tasks as directed.

The Geochemical Golem remains in this form for the duration of the spell or until it drops to 0 hit points, at which point it crumbles back into the earth. If the golem is ever more than 100 feet away from you, it continues to follow the last command you gave it.

Elemental Infusion (page 62): You can customize the golem's abilities based on the situation and your preference. You need to have atleast full worth of one element, to gain the effect. You can combine and mix the elements, if you want to.

Basic combination: You can combine up to two different elements for the base casting cost of the spell. The total cost would be the sum of the individual elements chosen.

Advanced combination: For additional element beyond two, you can add a third element for an additional 400 gp, the forth element for an additional 2000 gp.

annotated_entries.components: V, S, M (a handful of soil)
annotated_entries.description:
You form a deep connection with the land around you, merging your consciousness with the natural world. For the duration, you gain the ability to manipulate natural features within a 1-mile radius of your location. You can cause the following effects:

Alter Terrain. You can raise or lower the terrain, creating hills, ditches, or flat land. The maximum height or depth is 10 feet per minute. This does not affect buildings or other structures.

Divert Water. You can change the course of rivers or streams, or dry them up entirely. You can also create springs in places where water is close to the surface.

Grow Vegetation. You can cause plants to grow rapidly. This can create thickets or clearings in forests, or cause crops to grow in fields. The plants grow naturally and require suitable conditions to survive.

You have no control over animals, weather, or any unnatural constructs within the area. Any changes you make using this spell are permanent and occur naturally, though they may be startling or disruptive to those who witness them.
annotated_entries.higher_levels:
When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th level or higher, the radius of your control extends to 2 miles, and the speed at which you can alter terrain doubles.

When you cast this spell using a 9th level spell slot, the radius of your control extends to 3 miles, and the speed at which you can alter terrain triples. Additionally, you gain the ability to cause minor seismic activity, such as tremors, within the area of your control. These tremors aren't strong enough to cause damage but can be used to create distractions or unsettle creatures in the area.

annotated_entries.name: Neodrakite Net
annotated_entries.components: V, S, M (a net woven with threads infused with neodrakite worth at least 500 gp, which the spell consumes)
annotated_entries.description:
You create a shimmering net of rare earth elements and hurl it at a creature that you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be restrained for the duration. The net has no effect on creatures that are formless, or creatures that are Huge size or larger. The restrained creature can use its action to make a Strength check against your spell save DC.

Once ensnared, the neodrakite in the net begins to contract, exerting a crushing force on the restrained creature. At the start of each of its turns, the restrained creature takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage and the DC to escape the net increases by 1. The restrained creature can use its action to make a Strength check against the current DC. On a success, it frees itself.
annotated_entries.higher_levels:
When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th level or higher, the size of the creature that the net can restrain increases by one size category for each slot level above 7th. At 9th level, the net can restrain Gargantuan creatures.

Additionally, the damage dealt at the start of the restrained creature's turns increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 7th.
annotated_entries.source_notes: The spell-list index on PDF page 40 calls this Neodymium Net; the body heading and material text on page 70 say Neodrakite Net. The printed higher-level size wording is retained.

Each creature in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 12d6 radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The radiant energy is so potent that it continues to burn the target for 1d6 radiant damage at the start of each of its turns for the next minute.

The barrier moves with you, remaining centered on you and hedging out creatures that end their turn within 5 feet of you. They must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 bludgeoning damage.

For the duration, you can use your action to cause the land within a 500-foot radius of you to alter its form, creating new geographical features such as hills, valleys, rivers, or even small mountains. annotated_entries.name: Geomorph's Stone Sentence
annotated_entries.description:
You point at a creature you can see within range and attempt to turn it into stone. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is instantly petrified, its form becoming a lifeless, solid statue. If the creature has 100 hit points or fewer, it is instantly killed as its entire form is converted into stone.

If the creature has more than 100 hit points, it takes 10d10 necrotic damage as parts of its body begin to turn to stone, and it is restrained. The creature must make another Constitution saving throw at the end of its next turn. If it fails, it is petrified. If it succeeds, the spell ends and the creature is no longer restrained.

A creature petrified by this spell remains in its stony state until freed by the greater restoration spell or other magic. Additionally, if the creature has 200 hit points or fewer, it is instantly killed and turned to stone. If the creature has more than 200 hit points, it is restrained and must make the additional Constitution saving throws as described above.

The target takes 2d10 necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns as its body begins to harden and petrify.

The target has disadvantage on Strength-based weapon attack rolls due to the increasing weight and stiffness of its body.

Additionally, all allies within range receive a protective earth shield, reducing the damage they take by 15%. The deflected damage is dealt to the target.

decisions.name: Breeze Whisper
decisions.decision: Keep the short-message concept as a Mystic cantrip. Define delivery and failure without turning it into a creature-location oracle.

conversion.name: Breeze Whisper
conversion.components: Verbal, somatic
conversion.effect:
Whisper a message of up to twenty-five words to a creature whose voice you know. The creature must be within range, but you do not need to see it. A faint current of air carries your words around corners and through openings to the recipient, which hears them as a whisper. It can immediately whisper one reply of up to twenty-five words along the same route. The spell does not translate either message.

An open route through air must connect you and the recipient. The current cannot pass through a solid barrier or an area that prevents sound. A creature that cannot hear receives no message. If the recipient is absent, out of range, unreachable, or chooses not to reply, you receive no reply and learn no reason for the silence.
conversion.design_notes: The Mystic category follows the review. The air route, audible delivery, language limit and indistinguishable failure are proposed clarifications; the original uses mental delivery. Range and word limits are preserved. No combat bonus or automatic location information is granted.

questions: Should delivery remain mental as in the source, or use the proposed audible wind-whisper?

decisions.name: Gemstone's Glee
decisions.decision: Draft an Oath light cantrip with a utility guiding-mark option. Distinguish it from the existing gemstone recovery cantrip and separate Light hex.

conversion.name: Votive Gem
conversion.components: Verbal, somatic, material (a gemstone, which is not consumed)
conversion.effect:
Bless a gemstone you touch. It sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for a further 20 feet, in a colour you choose. Covering the gemstone with an opaque object covers its light.

A creature holding the blessed gemstone can use an action to touch it to a surface and trace a luminous sign no larger than a handspan: a simple arrow, warning symbol, or up to five written words. The sign glows visibly in darkness but does not illuminate its surroundings. Up to three signs made by this casting can exist at once; making another erases the oldest. They last until the spell ends and confer no automatic understanding, protection, check bonus or other magical effect.
A gemstone with this enchantment can function as an spellcasting focus akin to a crystal ball while held, and does not require attunement.
Only one gem can be enchanted in this manner by you at a time. Casting the cantrip again ends your previous casting and its signs. You can also end your casting as a bonus action while touching its gemstone.
conversion.upgrades: At 5th and 9th character level, increase both the bright-light radius and the additional dim-light distance by 10 feet, and increase the number of simultaneous signs by one.
conversion.design_notes: The guiding signs, their limits, the one-active-gem limit, proposed name and character-level upgrades are utility proposals to complete the review's request for a secondary option. They add no reaction or combat bonus. Innervate consumes a gemstone worth at least 50 gold to recover health and a rest die; it does not create light. The existing Light minor hex also enhances projectiles, which this proposal does not do.

related_spells.name: Light

questions: Is leaving simple guiding signs an appropriate secondary option for this light cantrip?
Keep the proposed Votive Gem name, or retain Gemstone's Glee?
decisions.final-answer: I eddited the description with a focus use part. otherwise approved, name is good. secondary effects are good too. upgrades should be as is.

decisions.name: Geomorpher's Compass
decisions.decision: Rename to Compass and move to Mystic 1. Spend a slot for one fixed destination, with finite sensing range and no distance or route information.

conversion.name: Compass
conversion.components: Verbal, somatic, material (a small iron needle, which is not consumed)
conversion.effect:
While touching the ground, name one stationary place on your current plane that you have personally visited or directly observed well enough to distinguish it from other places. A name, rumour, or imagined description alone is insufficient. Spend a spell slot and attune the needle to that one destination.

If the destination lies within 10 miles, the needle points along the direct horizontal bearing from you to it. It updates as you travel for the duration, but gives no distance, elevation, safe route, information about obstacles, or information about what is at the destination. It does not point to a person, creature, portable object, or a place defined by the presence of one.

If the destination is invalid, outside the spell's sensing range, on another plane, or protected from this divination, the needle gives no bearing. These failures are indistinguishable. The destination cannot be changed during the casting; choosing another place requires another casting and another slot. The spell ends if the destination moves or you cease touching the ground.
conversion.higher_levels: Each spell-slot level above 1st adds 10 miles to the sensing range. The casting time, duration and one-destination limit remain unchanged.
conversion.design_notes: The review explicitly requests Mystic 1, a simpler name and meaningful range. The 10-mile base range, one-minute casting, known-place requirement, concentration duration and indistinguishable failures are proposed safeguards against repeated free location queries. The spell still deliberately provides true directional information about an eligible known destination.

questions: Is 10 miles a useful level-1 sensing range, with a further 10 miles per higher slot?
Must the caster have personally visited the destination, or is the proposed direct-observation alternative acceptable?
decisions.final-answer: A lvl 1 find spell is interesting. I think the range should be 100 miles, and should jump unevenly. A 3rd spell slot should give 1000 miles, while a 5th slot should give 5000 miles.

decisions.name: Lithoresonance

conversion.components: Verbal, somatic, material (a natural stone or crystal suitable for the chosen mode, which is not consumed)
conversion.range: Touch; sound ranges vary by mode
conversion.effect:
Spend a spell slot and attune one stone or crystal by touching it throughout the ritual. Choose one mode permitted by the slot used. Only one object can carry your Lithoresonance at a time; completing another casting ends your previous one. An object whose mode requires it to remain in place loses its enchantment if moved.

* Whisper pebble. Place a pebble on a solid surface. The first Small or larger creature to move across the same connected surface within 10 feet of it causes the pebble to ring for one round, audible within 60 feet, then become inert. Creatures that touched the pebble during the ritual do not trigger it. It detects movement through the surface, not thoughts, identities, flight, or creatures standing still.
* Noise stone. Record one sound or spoken message of up to twenty-five words during the ritual. A creature touching the stone can use an action to tap it thrice, makeing it sound out the recorded sound. It comes out as crackling, deep, and with an earthy tembre (Subject to GM.)
* Thunder rock. Prepare one pebble or piece of stone ammunition. The first time it strikes a creature or solid surface after being thrown or launched, it gives off a crack audible within 300 feet and becomes inert. Creatures within 5 feet of the impact must make a Constitution save against your spell DC, becoming deafened until the start of your next turn on a failure. Resolve any weapon attack and its damage normally; this mode grants no extra impact damage.

All sounds are audible warnings or signals, not mental messages. Sound-blocking effects prevent a sound from crossing their boundary. The spell cannot force a creature to notice or interpret a sound when it could not normally hear it.
conversion.higher_levels:
Higher slots retain all lower-level choices and add the following modes:

* 2nd level: Stone gong. Enchant a stationary boulder at least 3 feet across. Set up to three distinct tones during the ritual. A creature touching it can use an action to sound one tone, audible in the open air within 1 mile. It transmits no words or private information.
* 3rd level: Crystal resonance. Enchant a stationary natural crystal formation at least 2 feet across. It hums audibly within 30 feet. Creatures you designated by touching them during the ritual gain a +1 bonus to block checks and saves made to resist being shoved, dragged, or knocked prone while they can hear the hum, are within 30 feet of the crystal, and stand on the same connected solid surface. Leaving that area suspends the benefit. Multiple Crystal resonance effects do not stack.
* 4th level: Mountain saga. Enchant a stationary natural stone outcrop at least 10 feet across. While touching it, you can use an action to make it sound a signal or repeat up to twenty-five words you speak aloud. The sound can be heard in the open air within 5 miles. A 5th-level slot increases this distance to 20 miles; a 6th-level slot increases it to 100 miles. Ordinary enclosed spaces and magical sound barriers can still prevent a creature from hearing the broadcast.
conversion.design_notes: Mode names and the first four slot tiers follow the review's outline. Trigger sizes, active-object limit, ritual slot expenditure, sound distances, Thunder rock's brief deafening, Crystal resonance's defensive aura and Mountain saga's 4th-6th level effect are proposed completions. No mode grants an automatic social-check success or psychic alarm. The level-3 aura should be compared with Geomancy's existing Crystal resonance option before acceptance.
conversion.final-answer: Approved with minor changes to noise stone. Crystal resonance should actually have a different effect. I think it should instead grant structures it is part of or attached to a +1 bonus to saves and resistance to damage.

conversion.name: Resounding Rebuke
conversion.components: Verbal
conversion.duration: Until the start of your next turn
conversion.effect:
Speak an oath of arrest in a ringing voice. Every other creature within 10 feet that can hear you, including allies, must make a Wisdom save against your spell DC. On a failure, it is stunned until the start of your next turn. On a success, it is unaffected. A creature that cannot hear you is unaffected.

questions: Is any area stun appropriate at Oath 1 under the current Stunned condition, or should this effect use a higher slot or a weaker condition?

decisions.final-answer:
Approved but with the following changes: * Change its range to be 30ft, but allow it to target creatures the target is familiar with. Since it is a word spell, it should be word based, allowing you to target creatures behind you and so on as long as you know they are there. Arguably the knowing shouldnt even be required. * The spell should target a single creature, but the  caster must know the name of the creatures kind or its actual name. * If the caster knows the creatures actual name, there should be a DC bonus of +2.(advantage is too high.) * Increase range by 5ft per slot level. * Allow targeting an extra creature per slot lvl above 2nd level, but only allowing you to address their kinds name(elves, bandits, witches, gnolls, King Hadvards sons, etc.) and ignoring those that are not of that kind.  * Change name to something like Rebuke thy Name. * Add 1d3 rounds to duration if the target rolls 5 or lower.
special designer note: The purpose should be to emphasise the logos and contract-like nature of Oath magic. A basic aoe stun is a bit more of a blast spell, even if it has no damage.

conversion.components: Verbal, Somatic, Material (an existing stone object or stone surface that is touched)
conversion.effect: Touch a nonmagical stone object or continuous stone surface. Grow one attached extension fitting inside a 5-foot cube, such as a step, support, simple barrier, bridge segment or blunt tool. The extension must remain attached to the touched stone when formed, must fit in unoccupied space and cannot grow inside a creature or object. It cannot create machinery, writing, precious minerals or a magically enhanced weapon. Its AC is 10 + your casting bonus and its HP is 10 times the sum of your character level and casting bonus, with a minimum of 10 HP. Damage affects the extension rather than the original stone unless an effect also reaches that stone. When the spell ends, the added stone crumbles into ordinary dust; the original stone remains. conversion.design_notes: The review specifies Mystic 3 and favors extending stone structures. Attachment, temporary material, unoccupied space and simple shapes are proposed limits. The source HP formula lacked parentheses; this proposed version explicitly chooses 10 times (character level + casting bonus), without changing the preserved original.

conversion.name: Bloomheal
conversion.components: Verbal, Somatic, Material (an emerald worth at least 500 gold, held against the target)
conversion.effect: Touch a willing living creature and stimulate its natural healing. It immediately regains 4d8 + casting bonus HP, then regains 1 HP at the start of each of its turns while the spell continues. If you maintain concentration for the full 2 minutes, the target regrows any limbs, digits or other ordinary body parts lost before the casting. A severed part held against its matching wound instead reattaches when the spell is cast. The spell cannot revive a dead creature, replace a missing soul, or remove a disease or curse.
