decisions.name: Crystal Prison
decisions.decision: Draft the requested Arcane 5 prison with defined escape rules instead of importing an indefinite restraint with no exit procedure.

conversion.name: Crystal Prison
conversion.components: Verbal, Somatic
conversion.effect: Choose one Large or smaller creature you can see within range. It makes a Dexterity save against your spell DC. On a failure, a cage of sharp crystal forms around it: it is Snared, and takes 4d6 piercing damage at the start of each of its turns. It can use an action to attempt a Strength check against your spell DC, breaking the cage and ending the spell on a success. The cage can also be attacked; it has AC 15 and 40 HP. Destroying it ends the spell without dealing extra damage to the prisoner. The cage permits air and sight and does not block spells or attacks that otherwise have a clear path through its gaps. A creature that teleports out of the cage escapes and ends the spell. On a successful initial save, no cage forms and the creature takes no damage.
conversion.higher_levels: When cast using a 6th-level spell slot, the ongoing damage increases to 5d6 piercing damage and the cage has 60 HP.
conversion.design_notes: The review specifies Arcane 5. Snared uses the current movement condition rather than assuming a 5e Restrained condition. Large-or-smaller targeting, an action-based Strength escape, cage AC/HP and teleport escape are proposed completions of missing source procedures. Reaching 0 cage HP never causes an additional burst.

conversion.effect: Choose a continuous area of natural earth or stone you can see within range, up to 100 feet across. Reshape its upper surface into one broad hill, ridge, terrace or plateau up to 100 feet higher than its original surface. The new surface must remain attached to and supported by the surrounding ground. Creatures on it are carried with the surface into unoccupied space without falling or taking damage from the reshaping itself; if no such arrangement is possible, that part of the ground is unchanged. The spell cannot be centered inside a constructed building, move manufactured structures, crush buried creatures, or grow through an existing solid barrier. conversion.components: Verbal, Somatic, Material (a hand-held polished mirror)
conversion.effect: Enchant a mirror held in one of your hands. conversion.name: Geomantic Ascendancy
conversion.components: Verbal, Somatic, Material (an earth-encrusted diamond worth at least 5,000 gold, which is consumed)
conversion.effect: Attune your body to the earth. For the duration, while touching natural earth or stone, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, slashing, acid, cold, fire and lightning damage; you can move through nonmagical natural earth and stone at a speed of 20 feet without leaving a tunnel; you sense the location of moving creatures touching the same continuous ground within 60 feet, although this sense does not let attacks or spells pass through barriers; and you can speak with and understand earth elementals. You must finish each turn in an unoccupied space outside solid material. If the spell ends while you are inside solid material, you are forced along the shortest route through material this spell permits you to enter to the nearest unoccupied space outside it; resolve equally short routes toward your entry route. Take falling damage as though you had fallen twice the distance you were forced to move. You do not become an elemental, gain immunity to damage, or pass through metal, worked masonry or magical barriers.
conversion.design_notes: The reviewer suggests Mystic 6 with clearer numbers and likes the single-paragraph form. Concentration, resistance instead of immunity, the enumerated damage types, natural-material limits and 20-foot speed are proposed balance and clarity decisions. Forced exit follows the existing Varis Ethereal condition convention, matching the Earthwalk draft: nearest unoccupied space by the shortest permitted route, with falling damage based on twice the forced distance. Unlike Earthwalk, this draft still requires ending each turn outside solid material. The costly consumed diamond is retained. No free ritual casting is granted because current slot-free ritual rules for this new draft have not been confirmed.
